title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Forecasting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Playbook
author: Natalie Singh
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standardized processes for budgeting and forecasting, procurement and vendor onboarding, contracts and legal review, and revenue recognition/billing. It is intended for finance business partners, procurement, legal, engineering managers, and product owners who request spend, enter contracts, or require billing/rev-rec guidance.

Scope

- Applies to all commercial and operational spend for Redwood Inference (hosted, dedicated and private product lines).
- Covers annual budgeting, rolling forecasts, purchase approvals, vendor onboarding, standard contract lifecycle, and ASC 606-aligned revenue recognition guidance for hosted usage and reserved capacity.
- Does NOT replace customer-specific contract negotiation guidance maintained in the Legal Contract Repository. For customer-sensitive details, see related restricted pages.

Ownership and RACI (high-level)

- Finance (Budget Owner): overall budgeting cadence, consolidated forecasts, financial policy, rev-rec guidance.
- Procurement: vendor evaluation, PO issuance, vendor master data, and preferred supplier management.
- Legal: contract template maintenance, risk reviews, NDAs, and approval for non-standard terms.
- Requesting Team (Eng/Product): initiates spend requests, provides business justification, and tracks deliverables.
- IT/Security: security and data residency review for private deployments and on-prem solutions.

Budgeting cadence and templates

1. Annual Budget Cycle (timeline):
   - July–August: Headcount and strategic initiatives planning.
   - September: Department-level proposed budgets due.
   - October: Finance consolidation and leadership review.
   - November: Board-approved working budget finalized.

2. Rolling 12-month Forecast: updated monthly; re-forecast drivers include new sales bookings, churn, runway, and material contract amendments.

3. Templates and required artifacts (attach to budget submission):
   - Budget worksheet (CSV) with line items: FTE, infrastructure (GPU hours), external vendors, marketing, travel, one-time projects.
   - Initiative memo (one-page) for line items > $250k CAPEX/OPEX.
   - Cost assumptions and unit economics (per-token / per-GPU-hour) for model serving workloads.

Forecast assumptions guidance

- Hosted API usage assumptions: report expected monthly active API tokens, median sequence length, and expected average tokens per request. These feed the cost model for cloud GPU hours and egress.
- Dedicated/Private contracts: include committed capacity (GPU-hours/month), expected overage rate, and any multi-region replication costs.
- Currency and FX: use USD baseline; local currency exposure must be reported separately.

Approval thresholds and procurement process

Approval thresholds (effective 2026-07-01):
- Up to $25,000: Manager approval
- $25,001–$100,000: Director approval + Finance business partner sign-off
- $100,001–$250,000: VP approval + Procurement + Legal review if contract involved
- Over $250,000: CFO approval required + Procurement lead + Legal

Procurement intake steps:
1. Requesting team files a Vendor Request Form (Confluence template + vendor questionnaire) and routes to Procurement.
2. Procurement performs vendor risk check (security, financial health, SSO/SaaS posture) and classifies vendor: Preferred / Standard / High-risk.
3. For software or cloud vendors: Procurement requests SOC2 report and data processing addendum (DPA) for any vendor processing customer data.
4. Procurement issues Purchase Order (PO) once approvals complete and vendor master is created.

Vendor onboarding checklist (required):
- W9 or equivalent tax form
- Banking details and contact
- Signed contract or SOW (if applicable)
- Security questionnaire / SOC report (if handling customer data)
- Insurance certificates for professional liability if required

Contracts and legal process

Standard contract types:
- Master Services Agreement (MSA) + Statement of Work (SOW) for Dedicated/Private deployments and large enterprise deals.
- Standard SaaS Terms of Service for Hosted API customers.
- Third-party licensing agreements for middleware or model IP.

Contract lifecycle steps:
1. Intake: Business owner opens a Contract Request Ticket in the Contract Management System, attaches proposed commercial terms and negotiation points.
2. Legal review (Triage): Legal assigns risk level (Low / Medium / High) and determines if standard template applies.
3. Negotiation: Legal + Sales/Product negotiate. Changes to standard templates must be tracked; redlines go through Legal.
4. Approvals: Director-level finance sign-off for commercial deviations, legal sign-off for legal deviations, and VP/CFO for high-value or strategic contracts (> $250k total commitment).
5. Execution: signatures collected via approved e-signature provider and final contract archived in the repository.

Non-standard clauses that trigger elevated review:
- Data residency or cross-border data transfers
- Indemnity caps removed or unlimited liability
- Substantial changes to service levels or uptime commitments

Revenue recognition and billing policies

Principles: Redwood follows ASC 606 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers). Revenue recognition depends on performance obligations, transfer of control, and timing of billable usage vs. committed capacity.

Common product revenue patterns and recognition treatment:
- Hosted API (usage-based): recognized as performance obligation is satisfied (typically over time as tokens are delivered). Monthly invoicing; revenue recognized in the month usage occurred.
- Reserved/Dedicated capacity (capacity subscription): recognized ratably over the subscription period unless a material deliverable is deferred (e.g., upfront implementation services), which is recognized separately.
- Private deployment/Enterprise license + SOW: license and implementation separated where material; license revenue may be recognized at a point in time or over time based on transfer of control and contractual terms.

Billing cadence and invoicing rules:
- Standard hosted customers: monthly invoicing in arrears for usage and any overage charges. Net 30 payment terms by default.
- Dedicated customers: monthly or quarterly invoicing per contract (per SOW). For committed annual contracts, invoicing cadence follows the payment schedule in the contract.
- Prepaid credits: recognized as deferred revenue and amortized over the period credits are expected to be consumed or as consumption occurs.

Key rev-rec operational controls:
- Usage metering reconciliation: Engineering billing exports (comma-separated daily usage files) must be reconciled to invoices within 7 business days of month close. Exceptions > 1% variance require finance escalation.
- Customer credit memos and disputes: logged in billing system; disputes older than 30 days require VP Finance review.
- Cut-off and month-end close: usage with timestamps through 23:59 UTC on the last calendar day is included in the period.

Templates and example snippets

1) Budget line-item CSV header (required):
   account_code,department,project,description,amount_usd,capex_or_opex,justification,owner

2) Vendor Request Form (short example fields):
   vendor_name,contact_name,estimated_annual_spend,product_description,security_classification,requested_by,requested_date

3) Sample contract approval checklist (text):
   - Is a standard template in use? Y/N
   - Is there customer data processed? Y/N -> If Y, attach DPA
   - Financial commitment amount and term
   - Approval signatures attached

Operational runbooks and exceptions

- Emergency procurement (e.g., urgent cloud capacity during incident): Procurement may approve up to $50k in one-off spend with VP Finance notification within 24 hours; all emergency purchases must be retroactively documented and reconciled.
- Refunds and credits: Customer refunds require Sales + Finance approval; credits for billing errors under $5k can be approved by Director Finance, above that requires VP Finance.

Reporting and KPIs

- Budget variance reporting: monthly department-level variance (actual vs. budget) with explanations for any line-item >10% variance.
- Forecast accuracy KPI: target mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) <= 7% for revenue line items at quarter granularity.
- Procure-to-pay cycle time: median 7 business days from Vendor Request Form to PO issuance for standard vendors.

Change history and governance

- This playbook is maintained by Finance in partnership with Procurement and Legal. Changes to thresholds, approval routing, or rev-rec policy must be approved by the Finance Ops Council and communicated to stakeholders.
- Next scheduled review: 2027-01-15.
